summary.text: An active galactic nucleus is a compact region at a galaxy's center that emits a large amount of energy across the electromagnetic spectrum, and stars are not the source.
Its radiation is theorized to come from the accretion of matter onto a supermassive black hole at the center of the host galaxy.
Active galactic nuclei are the most luminous lasting sources of radiation in the universe, so astronomers can use them to discover distant objects.

facts.label: Standard model
facts.value: Cold material near the black hole forms a disc

items.prompt: Telescopes find a tiny bright patch at a galaxy's heart, shining from radio to gamma rays. What sets an active nucleus apart from a normal busy galaxy center?

options.label: It is made of one single giant star
It shines only in visible light
Its energy output does not come from the galaxy's stars
It sits outside the galaxy's center

items.explain: An active nucleus emits significant energy with characteristics showing the luminosity is not produced by the stars.

items.prompt: In the standard picture, what happens to cold material near a supermassive black hole?

options.label: It forms a disc that heats up as matter moves inward
It falls straight in without warming up
It is thrown out at once as a jet
It settles into a ring of new stars

items.explain: In the standard model, cold material forms an accretion disc, and dissipative processes move matter inward while heating the disc.

items.prompt: A disc glows mostly in optical and ultraviolet light, yet the nucleus also shines at higher energies. What can explain that?

options.label: The disc cools off and shifts to X-rays
Nearby stars add X-ray light of their own
Dust turns visible light into X-rays
Hot material above the disc boosts photons up to X-ray energies

items.explain: A corona of hot material above the disc can inverse-Compton scatter photons up to X-ray energies.

items.prompt: Our galaxy has a supermassive black hole at its center, yet the Milky Way is not called an active galaxy. Why?

options.label: Its black hole is too small to count
Its black hole is not active at present
Dust hides its nucleus from view
It has no black hole at its center

items.explain: The Milky Way's central black hole is not currently active, though it is believed to have been active about 8 billion years ago.

items.prompt: Which of these can change how a particular active nucleus looks to us?

options.label: How much dust blocks the view of the nucleus
How many stars the host galaxy holds
How far the galaxy is from the Milky Way
The color of the host galaxy's arms

items.explain: Observed traits depend on black hole mass, accretion rate, disk orientation, obscuration by dust, and jets.

items.prompt: Carl Seyfert described nearby galaxies in 1943. What was unusual about them?

options.label: Their nuclei were unusually dark and cool
Their stars moved in perfectly orderly paths
They were found only in radio surveys
Their bright nuclei showed unusually broad emission lines

items.explain: Seyfert described galaxies with bright nuclei that were sources of unusually broad emission lines, and active galaxies like these carry his name.
